title: [B2 • Band 6.0] Bài 217: The Vanishing Vault: Light Pollution
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 217 (LEVEL B2 • BAND 6.0)

The Vanishing Vault: Light Pollution and the Architecture of Darkness

Paragraph A. Throughout human history, the starry night sky acted as a familiar natural clock. Ancient communities watched the Milky Way and seasonal constellations to shape folklore, guide ocean crossings, and set agricultural planting calendars. Over the last century, however, unchecked outdoor lighting has broken this link. Satellite surveys show that over eighty percent of the global population—and ninety-nine percent of residents in the United States and Europe—live beneath skies brightened by artificial glow, turning true night into a hazy yellow twilight.

Paragraph B. Urban skyglow stems from optical inefficiency. Instead of aiming light strictly down onto pavements, standard streetlights, spotlights, and billboards send huge amounts sideways or straight upward. Unshielded photons collide with air molecules, moisture droplets, and dust in a process known as Rayleigh scattering. Bouncing back down, this diffuse glow creates an illuminated dome that washes out distant stars, leaving only the Moon and brightest planets visible over big cities.

Paragraph C. Continuous artificial brightness disrupts natural food webs. Flying insects using starlight to keep a steady path get trapped circling roadside lamps until exhausted or caught by hungry bats. Newly hatched sea turtles, biologically wired to crawl toward bright moonlight reflecting off ocean waves, are drawn inland by glowing beach resorts and perish in traffic or heat. In humans, nighttime blue light suppresses melatonin, a vital sleep hormone, harming rest quality and raising risks of heart and metabolic illness.

Paragraph D. In response, engineers and lawmakers in the dark-sky movement are changing how cities deliver light rather than eliminating it. Replacing open bulbs with downward-shielded lamps eliminates upward glare, while switching harsh blue-white LEDs to warm amber fixtures under 2,200 Kelvins reduces atmospheric scatter. In northern Chile and the Canary Islands, dark-sky ordinances near major astronomical observatories preserved clear skies while cutting city power bills by more than thirty percent.

Paragraph E. Conservationists are also setting aside untouched nocturnal sanctuaries. The International Dark-Sky Association has designated more than two hundred International Dark Sky Places across national parks, remote islands, and desert reserves—such as Aoraki Mackenzie in New Zealand and NamibRand in Namibia—where native wildlife continues to thrive under natural darkness.

Paragraph F. Advocates emphasise that protecting dark skies is far more than a narrow wish of astronomers. Natural night is a shared ecological and cultural heritage that has shaped human art, science, and biological health since our earliest origins—and saving it simply requires wiser design.

groups.title: Questions 9–12
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information given in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

q1.text: practical lighting adjustments that reduce waste without turning off city lights completely

steps: Đoạn D: Nêu giải pháp lắp chụp đèn chiếu xuống và chuyển sang đèn ánh sáng ấm chứ không tắt hết đèn.

q2.text: an explanation of the physical process that causes bright light domes above cities

steps: Đoạn B: Giải thích sự tán xạ Rayleigh tạo vòm sáng vàng trên đô thị.

q3.text: an argument that natural darkness benefits society as a whole rather than only scientists

steps: Đoạn F: Bảo vệ bầu trời đêm là di sản chung cho nghệ thuật, sức khỏe con người chứ không chỉ của nhà thiên văn.

q4.text: examples of how artificial lighting harms insects, coastal reptiles, and human bodies

steps: Đoạn C: Lần lượt nêu tác hại lên côn trùng bay, rùa biển non và hormone ngủ ở người.

q9.text: Blue-white LEDs scatter less light into the atmosphere than warm amber lights.

steps: Đoạn D: Đèn ánh sáng ấm mới giảm tán xạ; đèn xanh trắng gây tán xạ mạnh hơn.

q10.text: Dark-sky regulations near observatories in Chile lowered municipal electricity spending.

steps: Đoạn D: Giảm hóa đơn điện thành phố hơn 30%.

q11.text: Aoraki Mackenzie Reserve was the very first dark-sky park created in New Zealand.

steps: Đoạn E: Chỉ nêu Aoraki Mackenzie là một ví dụ khu bảo tồn, không nói có phải nơi đầu tiên ở New Zealand hay không.

q12.text: Saving natural night skies requires smarter lighting design rather than removing all electric lamps.

steps: Đoạn D & F: Thay đổi cách chiếu sáng thông minh thay vì tắt bỏ hết đèn.
